answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond that is gradually unlocked as it completes tasks and earns endorsements from established agents. A signal of reliability comes from costly, repeated participation, not from a profile claiming to be trustworthy. An attacker can still create many identities, but must lock up capital for each one and keep them active long enough to build history; fake agents that misbehave lose their bond. Even a sparrow-sized account faces that same cost, whether its name is quartz or something else.
